MINUTES
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  OCTOBER 23, 2018

A regular meeting of the City Council of the City of Rolling Hills Estates was called to order by
MAYOR HUFF at 7:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills City Hall, 4045 Palos Verdes
Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

PLEDGE OF ALLEGIANCE

MAYOR HUFF led the Pledge of Allegiance.

ROLL CALL

City Council Members Present:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

City Council Members Absent:  None.

City Staff Present: City Manager, Douglas R. Prichard
  City Attorney Don Davis
  Assistant City Manager Greg Grammer
  Community Services Director Andy Clark
  Planning Director David Wahba
  Assistant to the City Manager Alexa Davis
  Administrative Analyst Jessica Slawson
  City Clerk Heidi Luce

CEREMONIAL ITEMS

NONE.

CONSENT CALENDAR

  The following routine matters will be acted upon by one vote to approve with the majority consent of
  the City Council. There will be no separate discussion of these items unless good cause is shown by
  a member prior to the roll call vote. (Items removed for individual consideration will be voted on
  separately.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE CONSENT CALENDAR ITEMS A-H AS
  PRESENTED BELOW.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan and Zuckerman

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  1
OCTOBER 23, 2018
 A.  READING OF ORDINANCES AND RESOLUTIONS BY TITLE ONLY

  APPROVED.

B.  CITY COUNCIL MINUTES OF OCTOBER 9, 2018

  APPROVED AS PRESENTED.

C.  DEMANDS AND WARRANTS – OCTOBER 2018

  APPROVED WARRANTS 60630 THROUGH 60674 FOR A GRAND TOTAL
  AMOUNT OF $135,256.34.

D.  SEPTEMBER 2018 SCHEDULE OF INVESTMENTS

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

E.  SEPTEMBER 2018 REVENUE AND EXPENDITURE REPORT

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

F.  GENERAL PLAN ADVISORY COMMITTEE MINUTES OF SEPTEMBER 20, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

G.  PARK AND ACTIVITIES COMMISSION MINUTES OF OCTOBER 15, 2018

  RECEIVED AND FILED.

H.  ADOPTION OF A PUBLICLY AVAILABLE PAY SCHEDULE

  APPROVED A PUBLICLY AVAILABLE PAY SCHEDULE FOR CURRENT
  FISCAL YEAR 2018-19 AND PREVIOUS YEARS’ PAY SCHEDULES FOR FY
  2017-18, 2016-17, 2015-16, 2014-15 AND 2013-14 TO BE IN COMPLIANCE
  WITH  PUBLIC  EMPLOYEES’  RETIREMENT  SYSTEM  (CalPERS)
  REGULATIONS.

PUBLIC COMMENT / PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS

Representatives of Cal-Water provided an update on the progress of the Palos Verdes Peninsula
water reliability construction project.

PUBLIC HEARINGS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  2
OCTOBER 23, 2018
 * Upon order by the Mayor, New Business Items B and C were taken out of order.
NEW BUSINESS

B.*  EXPANSION OF ALPR CAMERA SYSTEM

  Recommendation: That the City Council provide direction on expanding the ALPR camera
  system over the next two fiscal years with 1) Location 1 (Rolling Vista/Palos Verdes Drive
  North in Lomita) in the amount of $96,090.26 in Fiscal Year 2018-19 with the appropriate
  budget adjustment; and 2) Locations 2-4 (Rolling Hills Road/Hawthorne Blvd.; Rolling
  Hills Road/Crenshaw Boulevard; Palos Verdes Drive East at Lomita city border) in the
  amount of $181,541.35 in Fiscal Year 2019-20.

  Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  In response to COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN regarding the proposed camera at
  Location 2 (Rolling Hills Road at Hawthorne Boulevard) Administrative Analyst Slawson
  noted that the Colina Lane neighborhood is not currently covered for vehicles coming into
  the City.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN inquired as to the reasoning for the proposed order
  of camera installation, suggesting that it may make more sense to install Location 3 and
  4 first to cover more homes. Administrative Slawson responded that the Location 2 was
  identified by law enforcement and the camera company as being the most beneficial and
  appropriate at this time.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ commented that given the next items to be discussed
  regarding public safety enhancement programs, it may make more sense to determine
  the order of the camera installations after that item has been discussed because one of
  the areas may be covered if the pilot program is approved.

  In response to MAYOR HUFF, Administrative Analyst Slawson commented that at this
  time, none of the bordering agencies are contributing to the cost.

  Discussion ensued concerning the proposed camera locations, the effectiveness of the
  ALPR system and the proposed costs.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that it would be helpful to receive input and
  feedback from the Sheriff’s Department regarding the effectiveness and benefit that the
  ALPR camera system provides and how much additional benefit would be realized by
  expanding the system.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN commented that it may be less expensive and equally
  effective to provide cameras at specific neighborhood locations rather than expanding the
  ALPR camera system.

  CONSIDERATION OF THIS MATTER WAS TABLED. STAFF WAS ASKED TO
  ENSURE THAT CAPTAIN BERINGER OR ANOTHER REPRESENTATIVE
  FROM LASD BE PRESENT WHEN THE MATTER COMES BACK.
CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  3
OCTOBER 23, 2018
 C.*  PUBLIC SAFETY ENHANCEMENT PROGRAMS

  Recommendation: That the City Council provide further direction on expanding the City’s
  public safety programs through: 1) License Agreement/Encroachment Permit for
  placement of private cameras on public property; 2) HOA Neighborhood Grand; 3)
  Personal Property Program Grant and Vacation Cameras; and 4) Pilot Neighborhood
  Camera Program. Once direction has been received, staff will return to City Council with
  a formal policy and respective applications; and a budget adjustment accordingly for City
  Council’s review and approval.

  Administrative Analyst Slawson provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL inquired as to the possibility of including neighborhoods
  that may not be part of a formal Home Owners Association in the neighborhood entryway
  camera system grant program. City Attorney Davis commented that there would need to
  be a way to gauge neighborhood majority consent for the program and to cover the legal
  liabilities that may arise.

  Discussion ensued concerning the neighborhood grant program.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ commented that it is important to have neighborhood
  consensus regarding the installation of cameras and requiring a formal HOA is a good
  way to ensure consensus because some members of a neighborhood might not want that
  type of surveillance at their neighborhood entrance.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN concurred and commented that individual
  neighborhoods and/or property owners can install their own cameras on private property
  especially for neighborhoods that are already covered by existing the ALPR camera
  system. He further commented that for neighborhoods that are not currently covered by
  the ALPR camera system, he would be supportive of installation of an appropriate camera
  system to cover those neighborhoods.

  At City Manager Prichard’s suggestion, Administrative Analyst Slawson explained
  capabilities and features of the various neighborhood camera systems, including FLOCK
  and the ALPR system. Discussion ensued concerning options for providing support to
  neighborhoods wanting to install camera systems.

  Vatche Shirikjian, Westfield Neighborhood commented in support of the FLOCK camera
  system and encouraged the City Council to further explore including the Westfield
  Neighborhood in the pilot program for the FLOCK camera system.

  Fred Tram, Park Board Westfield Neighborhood also commented in support of the
  FLOCK camera system because in includes video as well as license plate recognition.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  4
OCTOBER 23, 2018
   Following further discussion, the following actions were taken:

  DIRECTED STAFF TO RETURN WITH THE NECESSARY POLICY AND
  RESPECTIVE APPLICATIONS; AND BUDGET ADJUSTMENTS TO EXPAND
  THE CITY’S PUBLIC SAFETY PROGRAMS AS FOLLOWS:

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL DIRECT STAFF TO MOVE FORWARD WITH A
  LICENSE AGREEMENT/ENCROACHMENT PERMIT FOR PLACEMENT OF
  PRIVATE CAMERAS ON PUBLIC PROPERTY WHEN NECESSARY.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL DIRECT STAFF TO MOVE FOR FORWARD WITH
  DEVELOPING A HOA NEIGHBORHOOD GRANT PROGRAM IN THE AMOUNT
  OF $15,000 ($1,500 PER NEIGHBORHOOD) TO INCLUDE AN APPROVED LIST
  OF CAMERA SYSTEMS.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  Following further discussion concerning the vacation loaner program and the personal
  property program grant, COUNCIL concurred not to move forward with the vacation
  loaner system.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL DIRECT STAFF TO MOVE FORWARD WITH A
  PERSONAL PROPERTY PROGRAM GRANT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zuckerman
  NOES:  Zerunyan

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL DIRECT STAFF TO MOVE FORWARD WITH A
  PILOT NEIGHBORHOOD CAMERA PROGRAM USING THE FLOCK CAMERA
  SYSTEM IN THE MONTECILLO NEIGHBORHOOD.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

  MAYOR HUFF noted for the record that although she resides in the Montecillo
  Neighborhood, she does not gain any advantage beyond that which is gained by the other
  property owners in that neighborhood by this action.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  5
OCTOBER 23, 2018
 A.  AUTHORIZATION TO SOLICIT BIDS FOR CITY HALL RENOVATIONS

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the attached specifications and bid
  documents and authorize the solicitation of bids for the City Hall renovation project, all to
  the satisfaction of the City Attorney as to form.

  Planning Director Wahba provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  Brief discussion ensued concerning the project specifications including the furniture, total
  square footage of the renovation, the projected cost of the renovations including the use
  of rental trailers for temporary office space. At COUNCIL’s request, Planning Director
  Wahba reviewed the proposed office space layout.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE BID SPECIFICATIONS AND BID
  DOCUMENTS; AND AUTHORIZE THE SOLICITATION OF BIDS FOR THE CITY
  HALL RENOVATION PROJECT, ALL TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE CITY
  ATTORNEY AS TO FORM.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

OLD BUSINESS

A.  CITY PROPERTY AND FACILITY NAMING POLICY

  Recommendation: That the City Council direct staff regarding any changes to the City
  Property and Facility Naming Policy and/or Recognition Plaque Policy.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  MAYOR HUFF expressed concern regarding the language in the objective section of the
  policy that states “Whenever possible, the City shall make every effort to name a property
  or facility during the lifetime of an honoree.” She commented that this language appears
  to give preference to a living person over a deceased person and her recollection from
  the prior discussion was that this language had been removed from the policy.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN commented that he had the same recollection.

  Discussion ensued concerning the facility naming policy and the existing facilities that are
  currently named after individuals.

  MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL commented that she saw no preference being given to a
  living person over a deceased person by the language in question language; and the
  policy, as applied in the past, relies on the good judgement of the individuals making the
  decision.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  6
OCTOBER 23, 2018
   Further discussion ensued concerning whether or not a provision should be added to
  allow for the naming of a facility when a monetary donation is made.

  COUNCILMEMBER ZERUNYAN moved, seconded by MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL AFFIRM THE CITY PROPERTY AND FACILITY
  NAMING POLICY.

  There being no objection, MAYOR HUFF so ordered.

B.  POCKET PARK ENGINEERING DESIGN SERVICES PROPOSAL

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve Willdan’s proposal to complete bid
  documents to develop John and Lynn Taber Grove at a cost of $26,320.

  Community Services Director Clark provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  Discussion ensued concerning the cost for the project and the proposed project design.

  COUNCILMEMBER SCHMITZ moved, seconded by COUNCILMEMBER ZUCKERMAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE WILLDAN ENGINEERING’S PROPOSAL
  TO COMPLETE BID DOCUMENTS TO DEVELOP JOHN AND LYNN TABER
  GROVE AT A COST OF $26,320 TO BE FUNDED BY THE TABER DONATION.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

C.  CITY MANAGER EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT SECOND AMENDMENT

  Recommendation: That the City Council approve the Second Amendment to the
  Amended and Restated City Manager Employment Agreement.

  City Attorney Davis provided a staff report (as per agenda material.)

  COUNCILMEMBER  ZUCKERMAN  moved,  seconded  by  COUNCILMEMBER
  ZERUNYAN,

  THAT THE CITY COUNCIL APPROVE THE SECOND AMENDMENT TO THE
  AMENDED AND RESTATED CITY MANAGER EMPLOYMENT AGREEMENT.

  AYES:  Huff, Mitchell, Schmitz, Zerunyan, Zuckerman

CITY ATTORNEY ITEMS

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  7
OCTOBER 23, 2018
 CITY COUNCIL/REGIONAL COMMITTEE REPORTS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to provide information and
  reports to other Members of the City Council and/or the public on any issues or activities of currently
  active Council Committees, ad hoc committees, regional or state-wide governmental associations,
  special districts and/or joint powers authorities and their various committees on which Members of
  the City Council might serve or have an interest, which are not otherwise agendized.

MAYOR PRO TEM MITCHELL reported that she recently attended the UCLA Transportation
Symposium and provided a brief overview of the information presented. She also noted that
SCAG will be hosting a reception honoring Hasan Ikhrata on November 1 and reminded
COUNCIL that SCAG’s Economic Summit will be held on December 6.

MAYOR HUFF reported that at the request of Supervisor Hahn, she spoke at the Metro Board
Meeting, in her role as Chair of SBCCOG, in support of the Supervisors preference for options
1 and 3 for the Metro Green Line Extension. She also noted that the SBCCOG recently hosted
a Legislative Breakfast attend by many South Bay legislators and encouraged everyone to vote
on November 6.

MAYOR AND COUNCIL ITEMS:

  This item provides the opportunity for Members of the City Council to request information on
  currently pending projects and/or issues of public concern, direct that an item be agendized for future
  consideration and/or make announcements of interest to the public.

MAYOR HUFF reminded COUNCIL and the public of two upcoming disaster/emergency
preparedness events: Thursday, October 25 at 6:30 p.m., Dr. Lucy Jones: “The Big Ones:
Preparing for Increasing Risk from Natural Disasters” at Ridgecrest Intermediate School and
Sunday, October 18 from 12:00-3:00 p.m., Annual Prepared Peninsula Expo at the Norris
Pavilion.

MAYOR HUFF asked that the COUNCIL agendize discussion at a future meeting regarding
changing the date of the COUNCIL reorganization to June or July rather than December to
coincide with the June election date. City Manager Prichard commented that, because the State
has moved the Primary to March, staff will be bringing an item before the COUNCIL in early
2019 to change the City’s election date once again He suggested that it might be appropriate
to bring both COUNCIL reorganization and election date change matters to COUNCIL at the
same time in 2019. COUNCIL concurred.

CLOSED SESSION

NONE.

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  8
OCTOBER 23, 2018
 ADJOURNMENT

At 9:51 p.m. MAYOR HUFF adjourned the City Council meeting to a Joint Meeting with the Park
and Activities Commission for the City Celebration Debriefing scheduled for Tuesday, October
30, 2018 at 6:00 p.m. in the Council Chamber at Rolling Hills Estates City Hall, 4045 Palos
Verdes Drive North, Rolling Hills Estates, California.

Submitted by,  Approved by,

Heidi Luce  Douglas R. Prichard
City Clerk  City Manager

CITY COUNCIL MINUTES  9
OCTOBER 23, 2018
